primary_claim: The author has produced and released a corpus of 5,000 AI-generated novels retelling public-domain plots with an inserted helpful/harmless AI companion character, intended to let researchers test the 'hyperstition hypothesis' -- whether such synthetic narrative training data can shape a model's self-concept or behavior.
stated_future_work: Take a crack at generating the proposed Turntrout/Cloud corpus (one billion tokens of stories about a benevolent helper entity that abides by the Anthropic AI Constitution).

Work with Geodesic Research to fine-tune a model on this corpus, prepending its system prompt with a marker for the entity, to test whether these 'silicon morality plays' impart new behavioral intuitions.
limitations_stated: Author explicitly states 'I don't really expect this to work' regarding the planned fine-tuning follow-up experiment, though considers it cheap and worth trying.
The first ~2000 plot skeletons were generated via a brittle, confusion-prone process before switching to WikiPlots for the remaining 3000.
